title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: Goodwill Waiver of a Fee
content:
## Clause

When the applicant asks for it, the desk may cancel one Dangerous Goods Acceptance fee entry as a gesture of goodwill. A waiver always takes away the entire entry it refers to, never part of it.

## Checklist for one waiver

| Test | What must hold | Record relied on |
|---|---|---|
| Kind of fee | the entry is a late declaration fee, an amendment fee, a re-review fee or a withdrawal fee | the fee entry |
| Size | the entry's amount is not above the category's goodwill authority | the fee entry |
| Allowance | the customer's dangerous-goods goodwill waivers during the trailing 365 days number fewer than the category's allowance | the customer's waiver entries across all its acceptances |
| Timing | the request is made no later than the last day of the category's request window | the date the fee was booked |
| Once only | the entry has not been waived before | earlier waiver entries |

Goodwill never reaches the administration fee, any surcharge, a misdeclaration penalty or an inspection cost recovery.

## Counting the allowance and the window

- **Allowance window:** the 365 calendar days that end on the date of the waiver, that date included, taken across every acceptance of the customer.
- **Request window:** the last day is the date on which the fee was booked, advanced by the category's window length on calendar dates; a request on that last day is inside the window.

## Hypothetical boundary cases

The window length used here, 12 days, is invented. For a fee booked on 2026-04-03, the last day is 2026-04-15: a request on 2026-04-15 is in time, a request on 2026-04-16 is not. With an allowance of 1, a customer who received a goodwill waiver 200 days ago cannot receive another now; one whose last waiver was 400 days ago can.

## Point of judgement

**The fee exceeds the authority by a small margin — can part of it be waived?** No. A waiver covers a whole entry, and an entry above the authority is not within the desk's goodwill.
